column12: We would like a table for two.
column13: What are we having for dinner?
column14: We are sharing a pizza. What are you having?

column12: We are only open until noon today.

column9: used like I by a king or queen

column9: people in general

column14: He did not seem to care.

column14: It's odd, but that's not to say [=that does not mean] that it's bad.

column14: You're not always right.

column13: "Do you mind?" "Not at all."

column9: used to introduce a statement that adds something to a previous statement and usually contrasts with it in some way

column9: used in negative statements to say that something must happen

column9: to express (an opinion)

column14: Who says I can't do it? I can do anything if I put my mind to it.

column9: to give (an order) : to tell someone to do (something)

column13: She's the boss. What she says goes! [=you have to do what she tells you to do]
column14: "Let's try installing the program one more time." "Whatever you say —you're the expert."

column9: to pronounce (a word)

column9: to repeat or recite (something)
column10: We always say our prayers before going to bed.
column11: Can you say the poem from memory?

column9: to use written words to give (information)

column13: It says here that there will be a special guest at the concert.
column14: The instructions say to add two eggs.

column9: to show or indicate (something) by using numbers, pictures, etc.

column9: to express (a meaning, emotion, etc.) without using words
column10: She likes art that really says something.

column12: The look on her face said "I'm sorry."
column13: His face said it all. = His face said everything. [=his face showed how he felt]

column12: We could leave on any day—say on Monday.
column13: Let's say you're right, for argument's sake.
column14: Suppose you won, shall we say, one million dollars. What would you do with it?

column9: used to suggest a possible or approximate amount, value, etc.
column10: The property is worth, say, four million dollars. = The property is worth four million dollars, say. [=the property is worth about four million dollars]

column9: an opportunity to express your opinion
column10: Everybody had a say at the meeting.
column11: We won't make a decision until all members have had their say.

column11: The students want a greater say in decisions that affect their education.
column12: He had no/some/little say in the matter.

column9: used to express surprise, shock, etc.
column10: Say, isn't that your friend over there?
column11: Say, that's a wonderful idea.

column9: used to attract the attention of someone
column10: Say there. Can you help me?
column11: Say, do you want to see a movie tonight?

column9: used to indicate the place where someone or something is

column11: The kitchen is at the back of the house.
column12: He was sitting at the table.
column13: They left for Cambridge early and arrived at [=in] Cambridge before noon.
column14: The party will be at Susan's house. = The party will be at Susan's.

column12: His anger is directed at his brother.

column14: He looked directly at me.

column9: used to indicate something that is being tried or attempted

column13: I'm bad at cooking. [=I'm a bad cook, I do not cook well]

column13: people who are at risk

column14: What [=how much] does it cost?
